task.title: Persist the latest due recurrence through the CLI
task.objective: Complete issue https://github.com/Knosence9/project-vela/issues/919 by exposing atomic latest-due provenance persistence through a thin deterministic writable CLI adapter.
acceptance_criteria: Validate recurrence identity before storage access and parse revision, start offset, and caller cutoff as u64 values.
Delegate guarded selection and persistence to the kernel while preserving future write-free and finite-completion cursor semantics.
Emit deterministic compact JSON on success and one escaped diagnostic with nonzero status and no partial stdout on failure.

attempts.diagnostic: The focused CLI integration test failed because persist-latest-due was an unrecognized recurrence subcommand.
attempts.patch: Added CLI tests for successful persistence, future and finite boundaries, revisions, duplicates, invalid inputs, and selected corruption before dispatch existed.

attempts.diagnostic: Added validated command dispatch, read-write storage delegation to persist_latest_due_occurrence, stable failures, and deterministic response serialization.
attempts.patch: Implemented the command in crates/vela-dev/src/lib.rs and documented the authority boundary in ADR-0063.

attempts.diagnostic: Initial CodeRabbit rate limiting was explicitly rejected as review evidence. A later genuine review completed with no actionable comments or review threads, and exact head 2157a48e40e0d977001d5481e059c499e25f4ce9 passed the Rust quality gate.
attempts.patch: Reused one serializer for read-only and writable latest-due responses and kept all selection and transaction policy in the kernel.

outcome.summary: Operators can persist one latest-due occurrence atomically without the CLI reading time, generating identity, persisting skipped work, or widening scheduler authority.

verification.command: nix develop --command cargo run --locked -p vela-dev -- record validate corpus/development/0189-atomic-latest-due-recurrence-persistence-cli.json # result: valid development record
nix develop --command cargo run --locked -p vela-dev -- corpus inspect corpus/development # result: inspected 193 records: 193 valid, 0 invalid
Pull request 920 exact head 2157a48e40e0d977001d5481e059c499e25f4ce9 squash merge 6971adefff165a39df03ef49b045abbfd8c1081d

lessons: A writable adapter should preserve one kernel transaction rather than composing a read command with a separate exact-coordinate write.
Caller-owned cutoff makes the due horizon explicit and prevents the CLI from silently reading ambient time.
Shared response serialization keeps read-only projection and writable persistence observably aligned.
The command persists provenance only and cannot generate identity, materialize, dispatch, retry, grant permission, or execute work.
